globalNotes: All downloaded JPEGs were opened and visually verified. No baked-in UI text, captions, or labels.
The four ESA/Hubble images are processed telescope observations. The Milky Way asset is an artist’s concept and must be labeled as an illustration wherever presented.
Approximate galaxy diameters depend on which component is measured. Use approximate symbols and do not treat these values as precise boundaries.

esahubble.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
esahubble.requirements: Keep the complete credit wording visibly associated with the image; make online credit links active. Do not imply ESA/Hubble endorsement. Resizing and cropping are permitted.

nasa.name: NASA Images and Media Usage Guidelines
nasa.requirements: NASA permits factual educational/informational use, including Internet pages, with source acknowledgment and no implication of endorsement. The selected NASA Goddard illustration has no third-party copyright notice.

galaxies.name: Andromeda
galaxies.imageDescription: NASA/ESA Hubble photomosaic released in January 2025.
galaxies.alt: A long Hubble mosaic of Andromeda, with a glowing yellow center, dark dust lanes, blue outer stars, and jagged mosaic edges.
galaxies.credit: NASA, ESA, B. Williams (University of Washington)
galaxies.compositionNote: Extremely wide panorama, with visible jagged edges from individual observations. Use contain for the complete mosaic, or crop carefully for a tall card.

facts.label: Distinctive feature
facts.value: The 2025 Hubble mosaic resolves the light of about 200 million stars, giving astronomers a detailed record of Andromeda’s history of mergers.

galaxies.processing: Converted to WebP; uncropped. A reduced thumbnail is supplied for navigation.

galaxies.name: Triangulum
galaxies.imageDescription: Hubble mosaic of the central region and inner spiral arms.
galaxies.alt: Triangulum’s inner spiral arms, filled with countless stars, dark dust clouds, and bright blue nebulae.
galaxies.credit: NASA, ESA, and M. Durbin, J. Dalcanton, and B. F. Williams (University of Washington)
galaxies.compositionNote: This shows the central region and inner spiral arms, not the entire galaxy.

facts.label: Type
facts.value: Spiral galaxy without a central bar

facts.label: Distinctive feature
facts.value: The Local Group’s third-largest galaxy has no bright central bulge; its abundant gas and dust sustain active star formation.

galaxies.processing: Converted to WebP; uncropped. A reduced thumbnail is supplied for navigation.

galaxies.name: Whirlpool
galaxies.imageDescription: Hubble image of M51 and its companion NGC 5195.
galaxies.alt: The Whirlpool Galaxy’s two blue spiral arms and pink star-forming regions, beside its smaller golden companion NGC 5195.
galaxies.credit: NASA, ESA, S. Beckwith (STScI), and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)
galaxies.sourceNote: Use the current NASA Messier catalog’s approximate 31-million-light-year distance. The 2005 ESA image page retains an older estimate of 25 million light-years.

facts.label: Distinctive feature
facts.value: Its two sweeping spiral arms compress hydrogen gas, creating bright star-forming regions and young blue star clusters.

facts.label: Companion
facts.value: The smaller yellow galaxy NGC 5195 passes behind M51; their interaction may help make the spiral pattern prominent.

galaxies.processing: Converted to WebP; uncropped. A reduced thumbnail is supplied for navigation.

galaxies.name: Sombrero
galaxies.imageDescription: Hubble mosaic with updated processing, released in April 2025.
galaxies.alt: The nearly edge-on Sombrero Galaxy, with a bright white central bulge wrapped by a sharply defined dark dust ring.
galaxies.sourceNote: Avoid an unqualified spiral or elliptical type. ESA’s 2025 release explicitly notes features of both and an uncertain overall classification. The 50,000-light-year diameter is from the earlier ESA/Hubble image description.

facts.label: Type
facts.value: Galaxy with both spiral and elliptical features

facts.label: Distinctive feature
facts.value: Viewed only about six degrees above its equatorial plane, its dust-rich disk cuts a dark band across a brilliant central bulge.

galaxies.processing: Converted to WebP; uncropped. A reduced thumbnail is supplied for navigation.

galaxies.name: Milky Way
galaxies.requiredCaption: Artist’s concept of the Milky Way
galaxies.imageDescription: Unlabeled top-down artist’s concept from NASA Goddard’s Conceptual Image Lab, released December 2025. This is not an external photograph of the Milky Way.
galaxies.alt: Artist’s concept of the Milky Way viewed from above, with a bright elongated central bar and blue spiral arms on black space.
galaxies.credit: NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Conceptual Image Lab

facts.label: Our location
facts.value: Inside the galaxy, about 26,000 light-years from its center

facts.label: Distinctive feature
facts.value: The Sun lies in the Orion Arm. Because we observe the galaxy from within, external views of the Milky Way are scientific illustrations.

galaxies.processing: Converted to WebP; uncropped. A reduced thumbnail is supplied for navigation.
